sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of BNNS readwith Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking quashment of proceedings in crime No.248/2024 dated 14/06/2024 registered at Police Station-Neelganga, District-Ujjain for the offence punishable under Section 419, 420, 467, 468, 109,
120-B IPC, Section 3/4 Public Gambling (Madhya Pradesh) Act, 1976 and Section 66-D of Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008.

At the time of hearing, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1/State on instructions would submit that after investigation, the investigating agency laid charge-sheet, took the cognizance, committed the case to the Court of Sessions and the Sessions Court registered the case as S.T. No.41/2025 and charges have been framed.

Learned counsel for the petitioner/accused submitted that in the intervening night of 13/06/2024 and 14/06/2024 Police Station-Neelganga received an information from the informant regarding cricket betting and police raided the house of the petitioner situated at 19, Dreams Colony &
Mussadipura and found few people involved cricket betting and seized cell phone and cash etc.
Thereafter on the basis of Panchanama police registered FIR in Crime No.248/2024 dated 14/06/2024.
2 MCRC-10997-2025 Learned counsel for the petitioner/accused vehemently argued that if at all the police arrested the petitioner/accused and seized material, they can register FIR under Section 3/4 of Public Gambling (Madhya Pradesh) Act, 1976 and Section 66-D of Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008 only but the police have registered FIR under Section 419, 420, 467, 468,
109, 120-B IPC without making any allegation and those Sections are not attracted in the present case and making harassment to the petitioner/accused.
The police included the Section under IPC against the petitioner/accused.
Learned counsel for the petitioner/accused further submitted that if the proceedings in the Court of Sessions in S.T. No.41/2025 is not stayed, it causes prejudice to the petitioner/accused.

sentences.text:
A decision reported in 2001 2 ALD 716 (Putti Satyanarayana Rao vs. Inspector of Police, ACB,
Kakinana) it is observed that "it is respectfully stated that this observation cannot be construed as the Supreme Court having laid down as a matter of law that in every case, where the complainant is the investigating officer, the proceedings have to be quashed irrespective of the facts of the case.

sentences.text: It may be pointed out that this infirmity was treated by the Supreme Court as a factor affecting the credibility of the prosecution case, which is obvious from the observation of the Supreme Court this is the infirmity which is bound to reflect on the credibility of the prosecution case."

Learned counsel for the petitioner/accused pressing for stay of proceedings pending on the file of District & Sessions Judge in ST No.41/2025 stated that if the trial is going-on, it causes prejudice to the petitioner/accused and filed IA No.3389/2025.
Perused the application.
3 MCRC-10997-2025 In such circumstances, granted interim stay in favour of the petitioner/accused - Piyush Chopra in respect of FIR No.248/2024 dated 14/06/2024 registered at Police Station-Neelganga, District-Ujjain for the offence punishable under Section 419, 420, 467,
468, 109, 120-B IPC, Section 3/4 Public Gambling (Madhya Pradesh) Act, 1976 and Section 66-D of Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008 and the further consequential proceedings pending before District & Sessions Judge, Ujjain in S.T. No.41/2025 till 25/03/2025.
In the meanwhile, directed the police to serve the notice to second respondent and file a proof of service through Public Prosecutor.
List on 25/03/2025.
